name: Rainforest Trust Feasibility Awards
summary: Small awards to registered NGOs to close specific information gaps, such as a legal pathway or species surveys, before applying to create or expand a protected or conserved area. The page gives an average size of about USD 10,000.

eligibility.rule: Be a legally registered NGO authorized to work in the project country
Have proposed areas that are currently unprotected
Target globally significant CR/EN species, large high-integrity forests, or climate-critical (sub)tropical habitat.
Have government and Indigenous or community support, with relevant FPIC completed or planned
Proposed protection changes legal status and mitigates critical biodiversity and applicable carbon threats.
Have or establish a management plan and committee for sustained biodiversity conservation
Have or establish resource-extraction limits to prevent unsustainable use
Assess feasibility of creating or expanding a protected or conserved area by filling a specific information gap.

status.quote: Concept notes are accepted anytime, and reviewed within 1-2 months.

applicant_types.quote: All applicants must be legally registered, non-government organizations that are authorized to conduct work in the country of the proposed project.

geography.quote: Our primary focus is the tropics and subtropics but strong proposals from outside these areas that meet all other criteria will be considered.

access.quote: We only review applications submitted directly by eligible organizations, and we will work with you to refine your proposal if it aligns with our mission and priorities.

window.quote: Protected or Conserved Area Creation Feasibility Awards; Protected or Conserved Area Creation Awards of less than $250,000: These are accepted on a rolling basis and may be funded anytime throughout the year.

effort.quote: Submit a Concept Note through our online form.
If your concept note is successful, you will be contacted by a Rainforest Trust staff member and invited to submit a detailed application via our online portal system.

eligibility.quote: The Project Implementer must be a legally registered non-government organization and authorized to conduct work in the country of the project.
The proposed area(s) must be currently unprotected.

Protect globally significant populations of Critically Endangered and Endangered species (e.g. Key Biodiversity Area (KBA) and Alliance for Zero Extinction (AZE) sites); AND/ORiii, iv 2.2 Protect large areas of Tropical and Sub-tropical High Integrity Forests; AND/OR 2.3 Protect Tropical and Sub-tropical habitat critical for mitigating global climate change

The project demonstrates support from relevant governments (including Indigenous governments) and Indigenous Peoples and/or Local Communities, and that relevant Free Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) has been or will be properly conducted.
The protection mechanism, resulting in a change in legal status of the area during the course of the project, will mitigate critical threats to biodiversity and, where applicable, to carbon storage.
A management system (management plan and committee) is, or will be, in place that ensures positive and sustained outcomes for the in situ conservation of biodiversity.
Resource extraction limits are, or will be, established to prevent unsustainable use.

Rainforest Trust provides Feasibility Awards to assess the potential for creating or expanding protected or conserved areas. These awards are intended to address specific information gaps in conservation projects, as precursors to applying for a Protected or Conserved Area Creation Award.
